children.value: > Fact From Story: Allison Miller, a Virginia woman, lost her leg to the flu.
> > Fact From Story: As Miller would later learn, her influenza had caused bilateral bacterial pneumonia — which affects both lungs and is more severe than viral pneumonia.
> > > Fact From Story: Ultimately, doctors had to amputate Miller’s left leg above the knee — all while she was still in a medically induced coma.
> > > Fact From Story: This led to sepsis, which quickly turned to septic shock.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Sepsis and septic shock are serious health conditions that can lead to amputation.
> > Fact From Story: This year marks a decade since serious complications from the flu led to a life-changing loss for the Virginia-based communications director.
> > > Fact From Story: Thinking it was the flu or something I could get over, I kept waiting to turn the corner — like, this is the worst of it.
> > > Fact From Story: Miller was a healthy young woman when she came down with a sore throat and headache.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Healthy people do not expect to lose their leg to the flu.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Bacterial pneumonia is a serious health condition.
> Commonsense Knowledge: The flu can cause serious complications.
